name: Hidden Structural Problems in Attached Garage and Bonus Room ADU Additions

mainEntity.name: What hidden structural issues do ADU additions contractors in Los Angeles County commonly find when converting attached garages or bonus rooms into ADUs?
mainEntity.text: What hidden structural issues do ADU additions contractors in Los Angeles County commonly find when converting attached garages or bonus rooms into ADUs?

acceptedAnswer.text: When converting an attached garage or bonus room into an ADU in Los Angeles County, contractors frequently run into conditions that were never built to current code standards. Typical surprises include undersized ceiling joists or rafters, sagging beams, and foundations that are shallow, cracked, or missing proper reinforcement. It is also common to uncover unpermitted alterations, such as makeshift bathrooms, DIY electrical, or old gas line taps, all of which must be corrected and brought up to code for the ADU permit to be approved and finaled. Moisture problems are another major issue: garages often lack proper waterproofing and vapor barriers, leading to rot in sill plates or lower wall sections. ADU additions also require specific fire separation between the unit and the main house or any remaining garage area, which may mean adding fire‑rated drywall and upgrading doors. Insulation and soundproofing usually need to be completely redone to meet energy and comfort standards. A seasoned ADU additions contractor will insist on detailed site walks, opening small test sections, and building contingencies into the contract for structural reinforcement and code corrections. Expect some extra time and budget for these items and prioritize contractors who explain how they manage and price hidden conditions.
